Landed: Gerrit change 1935 merged as e278425d7a (LLM-Review +1, Verified +1, 0 unresolved).
CI ran the whole tree (including tests/interfaces) and returned SUCCESS:
https://github.com/navapbc/rebar/actions/runs/32320873008

Late-binding audit (two-sided, per the config.py split lesson):
1. Symbols MOVED - nothing binds to them on the executor module object. The only
   monkeypatch target on rebar.llm.workflow.executor anywhere in the tree is run_workflow
   (test_code_review_gate_session, test_code_review_provenance, test_gate_engine_cutover,
   runs._ex in test_agent_op_safeguard, and the string form in test_plan_review_cancel),
   and run_workflow stayed.
2. Symbols the MOVED CODE CALLS - the moved cluster is closed. Its only outbound names are
   its own siblings (STEP_CONTRACTS, contract_for, _schema_is_opaque, _field_is_opaque,
   _primitive_kinds) plus two lazy imports that were already absolute or package-level
   (from . import steps; from rebar.llm.prompting.prompts import get_prompt). No name is
   resolved through the executor module namespace, so no late-binding path was severed.
   The get_prompt patches in the suite target the prompts module, not executor, and are
   unaffected by the move.

Accepted ADVISORY (non-blocking) from the code review on patch set 1: the new comment above
the import in executor.py says the moved names are 're-exported via __all__', but the
mechanism that makes them resolve is the module-scope import binding; __all__ only governs
star-import and keeps ruff from flagging the unused re-exports. The wording is imprecise, not
wrong in effect. Left as-is rather than spending a second change cycle on a comment; worth
folding into the next edit that touches this import block.

compiled_state.description:
## Target
`src/rebar/llm/workflow/executor.py` — **790 LOC** on origin/main against the 800-LOC hard cap (10 lines of headroom).

Ten lines of headroom.

## How to do it
Read the file and derive the seam from the CALL GRAPH — do not take any hint above as the answer.
Extract a cluster of functions that already call each other and that share one concern. The commit
message must NAME the concern boundary you chose and why the call graph supports it.

## Constraints (inherited from the epic — all non-negotiable)
- Split along LOGICAL CONCERNS / ARCHITECTURAL BOUNDARIES, never mechanically to hit a number.
- NEVER raise the limit; `.github/module-size-limit.txt` is locked.
- No resulting file under 100 LOC; target 200-500 LOC each.
- Leave REAL headroom — landing at 798 recreates the problem (that is how Gerrit 1916 failed).
- Behaviour-preserving: existing tests for this area must pass UNMODIFIED. If a test must change,
  the split was not behaviour-preserving — stop and reconsider the seam.
- Serena `find_referencing_symbols` for references, THEN `grep` for each moved symbol AS A STRING
  (monkeypatch.setattr / getattr / importlib). Serena returns EMPTY, not an error, for `Any`
  receivers, so the grep is mandatory.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `src/rebar/llm/workflow/executor.py` is under the cap with real headroom, and every new file is >= 100 LOC.
- [x] The split follows an existing call-graph seam; the commit message names the concern boundary.
- [x] Behaviour unchanged: existing tests covering this area pass UNMODIFIED. BOUNDED EXCEPTION: a
      purely mechanical `<file>:<line>` prose citation inside a test docstring or assertion MESSAGE
      may be repointed when the move shifts the line it names. That is non-behavioural (it changes
      no assertion, no fixture and no import) and is NOT evidence of a bad seam; any change to an
      assertion, fixture, import or expected value IS, and means stop and reconsider the seam.
- [x] The CI module-size gate passes without touching `.github/module-size-limit.txt`.
- [x] `make lint` passes.
- [x] `make typecheck` passes.
- [x] `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` reports `new=0` and `increased=0`.
- [x] All references updated — verified by BOTH a semantic reference search AND a string grep.

## Chosen seam (derived from the call graph, 2026-08-19)

**Concern boundary: the step-kind I/O CONTRACT MODEL (declaration + static compatibility) vs the
RUN ENGINE (control flow, expression resolution, dispatch, recording).** The two clusters in
`executor.py` share no call edges.

*Cluster 1 (moves)* - `StepContract`, `STEP_CONTRACTS`, `contract_for`, `input_schema_for`,
`shallow_contract_check` -> `_schema_is_opaque` / `_field_is_opaque` / `_primitive_kinds`,
`_SHALLOW_COMBINATORS`. Internal edges only (`input_schema_for` -> `contract_for` ->
`STEP_CONTRACTS`). Consumers are the STATIC / edit-time surface: `editor.py`,
`editor_contracts.py`, `lint_refs.py`, and the interpreter's pre-dispatch input validation.

*Cluster 2 (stays)* - `new_run_id`, `_capture_nondeterminism`, `StepContext`, `StepResult`,
`ScriptedStep`, `STEP_REGISTRY`, `register_step`, `RunState`, `RunResult`, the expression
resolver, `static_order` / `_terminal_step` / `_guard_passes`, `run_workflow`, `_dispatch`,
`_step_record`, the snapshot TTL sweep.

The run loop NEVER calls cluster 1. The only cross-seam edge is `register_step` writing
`STEP_CONTRACTS`, so cluster 1 moves to a new `step_contracts.py` and `executor.py` imports it -
one direction, no cycle. Same pattern as this file's two prior splits (`recorder.py`,
`runners.py`): move the cluster, re-export the public names so every import point is unchanged.

### The COMPLETE re-export surface (one line per moved symbol)
`executor.py` re-binds at module scope EVERY cluster-1 symbol any consumer imports from
`rebar.llm.workflow.executor`:
- `StepContract` - constructed by `register_step`; already in `executor.__all__`.
- `STEP_CONTRACTS` - written by `register_step`; imported by `tests/unit/workflow/test_contracts.py:18`.
- `contract_for` - `test_contracts.py:18`, `tests/interfaces/store/test_workflow_scripted_steps.py:16`; already in `__all__`.
- `shallow_contract_check` - `tests/unit/workflow/test_validation_depth.py:15`; already in `__all__`.

Worked example: `test_contracts.py:18` reads
`from rebar.llm.workflow.executor import STEP_CONTRACTS, STEP_REGISTRY, contract_for`. After the
move `executor.py` carries
`from .step_contracts import STEP_CONTRACTS, StepContract, contract_for, shallow_contract_check`
at module scope and `STEP_REGISTRY` never leaves executor, so that exact line resolves unchanged
and the file is not edited. `STEP_CONTRACTS` binds the SAME dict object in both modules, so
`register_step`'s writes stay visible through either name.

`input_schema_for` is the one moved symbol with no import from `executor` outside `src` - its only
consumers are the function-local imports at `editor.py:168` and `interpreter.py:76` (verified by
`grep -rn input_schema_for` over the tree) - so it is repointed at `step_contracts`, not
re-exported. The private helpers have no consumer outside the moved cluster.

### Why the OTHER candidate clusters must NOT move
- **Expression resolution** carries the ONE `# read-via:` line budgeted to
  `llm/workflow/executor.py` in `tests/scripts/test_llm_seam_clean_heldout.py` (`_MARKER_BUDGET`,
  exact count 1). Moving it turns that budget RED.
- **`run_workflow`** is a live `monkeypatch.setattr` target (`test_code_review_gate_session.py`,
  `test_code_review_provenance.py`, `test_plan_review_cancel.py`).
- **`StepContext` / `StepResult` / `STEP_REGISTRY`** are read as MODULE ATTRIBUTES (`_ex.X`) across
  ~50 test modules, so nothing that binds to the module object moves.
- The Burr tripwire scans `executor.py` + `interpreter.py` for banned imports and the trigger-list
  prose; the moved cluster has no control flow and no third-party imports and the docstring stays,
  so the tripwire keeps its intended scope unchanged.
- `.github/complexity-baseline.json` has ZERO entries keyed to `llm/workflow/executor.py`, so no
  baselined symbol is relocated (checked before choosing the seam).

### Expected shape
`executor.py` ~790 -> ~655 LOC (below the 720 near-cap band); new
`src/rebar/llm/workflow/step_contracts.py` ~190 LOC (over the 100-LOC floor). Moved bodies are
byte-identical apart from imports.

### Verification (each command exits non-zero on failure)
- `test "$(wc -l < src/rebar/llm/workflow/executor.py)" -le 720`
- `test "$(wc -l < src/rebar/llm/workflow/step_contracts.py)" -ge 100`
- `git diff --exit-code origin/main -- .github/module-size-limit.txt`
- `pytest -m "not integration and not external" tests/unit/workflow tests/unit/test_plan_review_workflow_ops_seam.py tests/scripts/test_llm_seam_clean_heldout.py tests/interfaces/store/test_workflow_scripted_steps.py`
- `make lint`; `make typecheck`; `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check`
- Reference sweep: Serena `find_referencing_symbols` per moved symbol PLUS
  `grep -rn '<symbol>' --include='*.py' --include='*.md' .` for each name AS A STRING
  (monkeypatch.setattr / getattr / importlib); no site may still expect a symbol at its OLD home.
